s-loftin-lexington-1895-07-26.A2: Loftin, at 5:30 yesterday evening, who dangles from a tree one mile northwest of town for attempting rape upon Anna Minehardt Tuesday and Mrs. Krotchkike at Dimebox seven years ago, which crime he confessed. Anna Minehardt is the 12-year-old daughter of Jacob Minehardt, a farmer living six miles west of town, who was upon her way to school. Loftin would have accomplished his purpose but for some children, as Loftin thought they were men. Seven years ago at Dimebox he strangled Mrs. Krotchkike to death and then accomplished his purpose. She was found three days afterwards and the mystery has remained unsolved until yesterday, when Loftin confessed both crimes, for which he paid his life. A mob went from here Tuesday night to Giddings and got Lofting, who was carried there that day, after being caught two miles below Lincoln. The mob had very little trouble securing Loftin out of jail at Giddings, as their arrival was a surprise and they caught the jailer at 3 yesterday morning. No one suspected their intentions. Sheriff Scarborough got out his bloodhounds to find the party, but they eluded him and finished Loftin's career without law.

Electricity Saved Him. HOUSTON, TEX—Albert Hauff, a carpenter, took twenty-five grains of morphine Thursday. A physician was summoned and had him carried to an electrical power house, where 400 volts were sent through him, resuscitating him almost instantly. He will recover. The Post's annual children's day was a glorious one with the exception of the heat. About 10,000 people visited the grounds during the day. The goat race for the Lender's prize, was won by Black Bill, driven by Durward Bailey, Houston, driven by Jimmie Adair, was second. The prize calls for a trip to Pittsburg, Pa., offered by the Leader, of that city, with expenses paid, a racing sulky with a $75 tailormade suit of clothes and other things, aggregating in financial worth about $175. Counterfeiter Arrested. TEXARKANA, ARK.—William Jackson, an expert iron and wood workman, who has been working for about a month at Tom Estes' shop, was arrested on the Texas side Sunday evening on the charge of counterfeiting on a warrant sworn out before United States Commissioner Carman. Several pairs of molds and a sack full of counterfeit silver dollars were found in the prisoner's room. Jackson made his escape from the officers having him in charge by leaping a ten-foot fence. He is now in the woods on the Arkansas side with the officers in hot pursuit, and his capture is expected. Daring Down-Town Hold-Up.
NEW ORLEANS, LA.—A daring robbery was committed by Eugene Cotard, living on Royal, between Hospital and Ursulines streets, Saturday morning. Paul Maxwell, a boy of ten years, living at 185 Dorgenois street, was on his way to the Germania Savings Bank to deposit his savings, and carried his little iron safe in his hands. Cotard forcibly took the safe from the boy and ran to the cemetery on Esplanade street, near Bayou St. John, where he broke it open. He was arrested and said that he had divided the money with three other men.

Dodging the Lynchers.

CLARKESVILLE, TENN.—Jeff Hoover, who killed J. H. Parker, and Joe Wells, the slayer of Lock Carney, were brought here Monday from Stewart county by Sheriff Crane, who was warned that preparations were being made to lynch the prisoners. In each case the murderer is a wronged husband and the victim the alleged despoiler of his home.

Desperate Affray at Hot Springs.

Hot Springs, Ark.—D. W. Claiborne, a grocer, became involved in a quarrel, Tuesday afternoon, with Jim and W. C. Meyers, brothers. Buildings Collapse.

FORT WORTH, TEX.—Two large buildings, located on Moore and Terrill, collapsed and both are wrecks. Workmen were put in a new floor in one of the buildings when the crash came. At the one of the buildings was crowded people, it being a store, but all one without serious injury.

Fire Destroys Melrose.
Ottumwa, Ia., July 27.—Fire to-day destroyed ten buildings, including the bank, at Melrose, Ia.

Convicts Killed.
Little Rock, Ark., July 27.—Five negro convicts made a break for liberty this morning, as a result of which one Wallace McNeil is dead and another, named Turner, is fatally injured and at large, with blood hounds after him. A bunch of about 100 convicts were being taken from the penitentiary near the insane asylum, eight guards being in charge, when the fight occurred.

The United States cruiser New York has arrived at New York fgrom Kiel.
s-loftin-lexington-1895-07-26.A10:
WEST AND SOUTH.
DAISIE KLAUS, aged 13, daughter of Charles Klaus, of Columbus; May, aged 11, and Hulda, aged 7, daughters of George Klaus, were drowned in the Platte river near Columbus, Neb.

ARTHUR WALTER, Joseph Nolte and Miss Tillie Hein were drowned in the Mississippi river at Burlington, la., by the capsizing of a boat.

In the Illinois legislature a bill was introduced for a tax of 2 per cent. upon the gross receipts of all games of ball and to prohibit the game on Sunday.

The prospects for an enormous crop of corn and other products throughout the west and northwest were never more promising.

A mob lynched S. Loftin, a negro, charged with assaulting a white woman in Lexington, Tex.

WILLIE COOK, Tudor Brown, Sim Echols and John Armstrong, negro desperadoes who broke jail at Fernandina, Fla., were driven into the ocean by bloodhounds and all were drowned.

WYOMING advices say that fifty-nine white people were killed by the Bannock Indians near Jackson's Hole.

A mob took Tom Johnson, a negro who murdered Mrs. Hartfield and her daughter at Meridian, Miss., and assaulted another daughter, and burned him at the stake.

In a duel at Brandenburg, Ky., Col. George Robinson, a county official, was killed, and Maj. Blood Schacklett, a county commissioner, was fatally injured.

Most of the village of Melrose, Ia., was burned.

Whit Ferrand and Anderson Brown, negro murderers, were executed at Salisbury, N. C., in the presence of 5,000 people. Each confessed his guilt.

At Richmond, Va., Phillip Norman Nicholas was hanged for murdering William J. Wilkerson and James Mills by drowning them.

The execution of William Fredericks, who murdered William A. Herrick in an attempt to rob the San Francisco Union savings bank in March, 1894, took place at San Quentin, Cal.

In all, so far as known, circumstantial evidence of the strongest character points to H. H. Holmes, the insurance swindler, as the slayer of Julia Connor, Gertrude Connor, Amelia Cigrand, Benjamin F. Pitzel and his three children, Howard, Alice and Nellie, Minnie and Alice Williams and a Miss Wild. Mrs. Patrick Quinlan confessed in Chicago all she knew about Holmes, and she and her husband were arrested as accomplices.

It was found that Bob Haggard, a negro who was lynched at Ford, Ky., charged with having outraged Miss Elkin, was innocent of the crime.

During a violent hurricane on the coast of Japan, many vessels were wrecked and their crews drowned.

DISPATCHES say that every man, woman and child in Jackson's Hole, Wyo., had been murdered by the red men and the settlement burned. The place had about 140 inhabitants.

FLAMES destroyed the county insane asylum at Verona, Wis., and Superintendent Edwards was probably fatally injured.

At Spirit Lake, Ia., a monument was dedicated to the pioneers killed in the Spirit Lake massacre of 1857. Many prominent men of the state were present.

A mob lynched Charlie Burwell (colored), about 65 years old, at Meridian, Miss. It was thought that he was concerned in a murder.

For no cause known Henry Bradshaw, a wealthy farmer, near Paris, Tex., killed his wife and thenhimself.

The Oklahoma supreme court again declared that probate judges have no right to grant divorces, and that all divorces granted by them are null and void.

In North Dakota a hailstorm destroyed 80,000 acres of wheat, causing
IN North Dakota a hailstorm destroyed 80,000 acres of wheat, causing a loss to farmers of $500,000.

DISAPPOINTED in love Edward Kneven, of Dayton, Ky., fatally shot Mary Schneer, of Alexandria, Ky., in Cincinnati, and then shot himself.

The doors of the Superior national bank of West Superior, Wis., were closed with liabilities of $141,300.

In the vicinity of Three States, Mo., George McClelland and his wife and three children and a man named Thomas and his wife were killed by lightning.

In Thompson, Ia., forty people were poisoned by eating pressed beef at the home of George Griswold.

John Hicks' house was burned at Big Stone Gap, Va., and four of his children perished in the flames.

The governor of Texas issued a proclamation forbidding the Corbett-Fitzsimmons fight in that state.

CHARLES Lynch, J. W. Blundon, 13 years old, and J. Guy Brown, 15 years, were struck by an express train near Riverdale Park, Md., and instantly killed.

The death was announced of Mrs. Isabel McKeehan, of Washington county, Tenn., at the age of 112 years.

At O'Neils, Cal., Victor Adams, who shot and killed Justice Boker, his father-in-law, was lynched by a mob of sixty men.

The failure of the Jacob Katz company, supposed to be one of the strongest mercantile establishments in Milwaukee, for $110,000, was reported.

In Macon, Mo., forty prominent merchants were arrested for doing business on Sunday.

The News Condensed.
Important Intelligence From All Parts.
DOMESTIC.
Princeton, N. J., last June, was sentenced to twenty years at hard labor in the state prison.

CHARLES M. WEBB has declined the appointment of associate justice of the supreme court of Wisconsin.

THE city waterworks at Ironton, O. were burned, the loss being $100,000.

A NATIONAL association of wire goods manufacturers was formed at Cincinnati with Fred J. Meyers, of Hamilton, O., as president.

The third annual convention of the United States League of Building and Loan associations convened in Cleveland.

RAINS have put an effectual check to forest fires in Michigan.

Ten cars and an engine were smashed in a freight wreck at New Florence, Pa., and Fireman Peter Cover was instantly killed.

GRATTON G. WILLIAMS, paper dealer in Philadelphia, failed for $100,000.

DAISIE aged 13, daughter of Charles Klaus, of Columbus, May, aged 11, and Hulda, aged 7, daughters of George Klaus, were drowned in the Platte river near Columbus, Neb.

WILLIAM TAYLOR, a negro, aged 21 years, was executed at Columbus, O., for killing Farmer Yoakum to rob him.

By a decision of Judge Johnston all cigar stores in Columbus, O., will be closed on Sunday.

ALABAMA populists and free silver republicans will hold a joint silver convention in Birmingham in November.

ROBERT E. RIVERS, principal owner of the Pickwick and Royal hotels in New Orleans and of a half dozen sugar plantations, failed for $330,000.

EMELINE G. CIGRAND and her husband, Robert E. Phelps, and a young girl whose name the police refused to divulge were the latest to be numbered among the supposed victims of H. H. Holmes in Chicago. All three have been missing more than two years.

FIRE in Melrose, Ia., burned most of the village.

Two NEGRO murderers, Whit Ferrand and Anderson Brown, were executed at Salisbury, N. C., in the presence of 5,000 people. Each confessed his guilt.

The Central Labor union of Cleveland, O., decided to boycott all grocers and dealers who sell nonunion bread.

Advices from Wyoming say that fifty-nine white people were killed by the Bannock Indians near Jackson's Hole.

As a result of a duel at Brandenburg, Ky., Col. George Robinson, a county official, was dead, and Maj. Blood Schacklett, a county commissioner, was fatally injured.

The commissioner of internal revenue in his annual report for the fiscal year ended June 30 says the total receipts from all sources for the year were $143,245,977, a decrease of $3,922,-471 as compared with 1894.

PHILLIP NORMAN NICHOLAS was hanged at Richmond, Va., for murdering William J. Wilkerson and James Mills by drowning them.

Tom Johnson, a negro who murdered Mrs. Hartfield and her daughter at Meridian, Miss., and assaulted another daughter, was burned to the stake by a mob.

The secretary of the treasury directed that the money paid into the treasury on account of the income tax be refunded to the persons and corporations respectively entitled thereto upon the filing of the refunding claims.

The national prohibition camp-meeting commenced at Decatur, Ill.

Tudor Brown, Willie Cook, Sim Echols and John Armstrong, negro desperadoes who broke jail at Fernandina, Fla., were driven into the ocean by bloodhounds and all were drowned.

The exchanges at the leading clearing houses in the United States during the week ended on the 26th aggregated $726,665,760, against $1,030,030,049 the previous week. The increase, compared with the corresponding week in 1894, was 20.2.

Joseph Nolte, Arthur Walter and Miss Tillie Hein were drowned in the Mississippi river at Burlington, Ia., by the capsizing of a boat.

S. Loftin, a negro, charged with assaulting a white woman in Lexington, Tex., was taken from the officers by a mob and lynched.

A bill was introduced in the Illinois legislature for a tax of 2 per cent. upon the gross receipts of all games of ball and to prohibit the game on Sunday.

Prospects for an enormous crop of corn and other products throughout the west and northwest were never more promising.

It developed that the negro Bob Haggard, who was lynched at Ford. Ky., charged with having outraged Miss Elkin, was innocent of the crime.

There were 202 business failures in the United States in the seven days ended on the 26th, against 256 the week previous and 249 in the corresponding time in 1894.
Joseph A. Beam was hanged at the United States jail at Washington for the murder of his stepdaughter, Mrs Annie Leahy, last December.
SECRETARY MORTON has abolished the seed division of the agricultural department in Washington, to take effect
